title: Answer a request without spoiling it

blocks.text: The page turns a request into a response by changing it in place: a new MTI, a response code, the EMV data removed. That is a hazard in a client or server that still holds the request, to log it, match it or retry it, because after the call the request is no longer the request.
Write `ResponseMaker` with `respond(ISOMsg request, String responseCode)`. It returns a new `ISOMsg` that:

items: has the response MTI for the request's MTI: the third digit goes up by one, so a `0200` is answered with a `0210`;
carries every field of the request, with the same values;
does not carry field 55 (the chip's EMV data), whether or not the request had it.
Do not assume every request is a `0200`. An authorization `0100` is answered with a `0110`.
The request passed in must come out of the call exactly as it went in: same MTI, same fields, its field 55 still there, and no field 39 added to it.

cases.says: a 0200 request is answered with a 0210 that echoes its fields, carries the response code in field 39 and drops the EMV data in field 55
the response MTI follows the request's MTI, so a 0100 is answered with a 0110
the request is left exactly as it came in

concepts: An ISOMsg holds an MTI and values keyed by field number: set puts one, getString reads one, and hasField asks whether an optional field is present before it is read.
A response is built from its request by changing the MTI, adding the response code in field 39 and removing what must not travel back, such as the EMV data in field 55.
